test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the shape of a water pipe is a rectangle with dimensions 5 m and 3 m and if water runs out of it at the speed of 36 km/hr, then what is the volume (in m3 ) of the water that passed through the pipe in 12 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume = Area of cross-section × Speed × Time

Volume = (5 × 3) × (36 × 1000 / 60) × 12

Volume = 15 × 600 × 12 = 108000 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 108000 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dimensions of **rectangular pipe** = 5 m × 3 m

**Speed of water** = 36 km/hr

**Time duration** = 12 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Volume of water = **Area of cross-section** × **Length of water column**

Length = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3fc13793d8895a320c5a3d78901d7f544afbcc43dba25795d397a8af482d2bbc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of cross-section = 5 × 3 = 15 m²

⇒ Speed in m/min = (36 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 600 m/min

⇒ Length of water column in 12 min = 600 × 12 = 7200 m

⇒ Volume = 15 × 7200

⇒ Volume = 108000 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 108000 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Flow Rate Concept

The volume of liquid flowing through a pipe per unit time is given by **Area × Velocity**.

Unit Conversions

To convert **km/hr to m/sec**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m³ to Litres**, multiply by 1000.

Cylindrical Pipe Volume

For a circular pipe with radius r, the volume is πr² × speed × time.</p
